questions.prompt: Rotating by rotation vector a and then by b is, in general,
options: not equal to rotating by a+b; the error is of second order and involves a x b
exactly the rotation with vector a+b, since the vectors simply add
the rotation with vector a-b, since the second rotation undoes the first
the same as b followed by a, because rotations always commute
questions.explanation: SO(3) is non-commutative; BCH gives exp(a)exp(b)=exp(a+b+1/2 a x b+...).

questions.prompt: A rotation matrix has trace 2. What is its rotation angle in degrees?
Rotation vector (0,0,pi/2) (rad). What is the (1,0) entry of exp([w]x)? (row 1, column 0, 0-based)
questions.explanation: This is Rz(90 deg): second row first column = sin(90 deg)=1.

questions.prompt: a=(0.2,0,0) and b=(0,0.2,0). The BCH second-order term (1/2)(a x b) has what z-component?
Why does R <- R + R[w]x dt fail as a gyro integrator?
options: Skew-symmetric matrices cannot be multiplied with rotation matrices in this form
It integrates the wrong angular velocity; the body-frame rate must be used instead
It is too slow to compute, so the step must be replaced by a lookup of rotations
The result is not orthogonal: I+[w]x dt scales the columns by sqrt(1+(w dt)^2)
questions.explanation: The update leaves SO(3); use R exp([w]x dt).

questions.prompt: Twist with v=(1,0,0) m/s and w=(0,0,pi/2) rad/s applied for 1 s. What is the x-coordinate of the translation of exp(xi)? (3 decimals)
questions.explanation: The robot follows a quarter circle of radius 2/pi, so x=2/pi=0.6366.

questions.prompt: An error-state filter stores orientation as a quaternion but represents its error as a 3-vector and updates with exp. Explain why the error is kept in the tangent space, and how the update and covariance are handled.
rubric: Explains that the tangent space is a flat 3-D vector space where covariances and additive corrections make sense.
Gives the update R <- R exp(delta) (or q <- q * exp(delta/2)) followed by a reset.
Notes the choice of left or right perturbation must match the covariance convention.
